summary: Subtractive rectangle clipping. Computes the area of a subject rectangle (this[0]..this[3], a 16-bit x1/y1 plus extents) that lies outside a boundary rectangle (a2..a5). Splits the space into a 3 by 3 grid, allocates a resource-pool node per surviving cell, links the nodes into a singly linked list via the next-pointer at node offset 12, and returns the list head (0 when the subject is entirely inside the boundary).

local_names.this: subject rectangle: x1, y1, x-extent, y-extent (16-bit words), metadata at offset 8
local_names.v43: 3 by 3 grid of cell-mask bytes (live = allocated cell)
local_names.v45: sorted x coordinates of the 3 grid columns
local_names.v47: sorted y coordinates of the 3 grid rows
local_names.v34: linked-list head of allocated output nodes

operations.description: Read subject rectangle x1 (this+0) and y1 (this+2) and compute right = x1 + extent (this+4) and bottom = y1 + extent (this+6).
Build boundary coordinate arrays from a2..a5: columns v45 = (a2, right-derived, a2+a4) and rows v47 = (a3, bottom-derived, a3+a5).
Bubble-sort the 3 column coordinates (v45) and 3 row coordinates (v47) by running 3 passes of a 3-element compare-swap loop.
Build the 3 by 3 cell-mask grid v43: for each cell, record whether it lies within the subject rectangle or outside the boundary rectangle (inside-subject OR not-inside-boundary test).
For each not-yet-marked cell, test whether the cell spans positive width and height (column delta and row delta greater than 0); zero-size cells are marked as handled.
For each surviving cell, mark it and the cells it covers as handled, then allocate a clipped-rectangle output node via ResourcePoolNodeAllocDealloc(x, y, width, height).
Copy the subject metadata word from this+8 into the allocated node at node offset 8.
Append the new node to the singly linked list using the next-pointer at node offset 12, or start the list with it when the list head is empty.
Return the linked-list head of allocated clipped rectangles (0 when no cell passed the tests).

clean_pseudocode: right = x1 + this[2]; bottom = y1 + this[3];
cols = sort(a2, right, a2 + a4); rows = sort(a3, bottom, a3 + a5);
